chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim, from al-Harith, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no harm in delaying the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) until the new moon of Dhu al-Qa'dah."

This is understood to mean that if one does not find a recipient for it, there is no harm in delaying it; however, it is obligatory upon him to set it aside from his wealth and distinguish it at its proper time, and give it to the recipient when he is able to do so. This is clarified by what he narrated.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.هِلَالِ ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: The new moon of the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah
key_terms.يَعْزِلَهَا: To segregate or set aside (from other wealth)
key_terms.يُمَيِّزَهَا: To distinguish or separate (specifically for this obligation)

ai.seo_question: When is the latest permissible time to pay Zakat al-Fitr if no recipient is immediately available?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) clarifying that delaying Zakat al-Fitr until the new moon of Dhu al-Qa'dah is permissible when no specific recipient is identified, provided the amount is segregated from one's wealth. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the purity of the funds and the obligation to pay promptly once the payer is able to distribute it, distinguishing between the general period of acceptance and the specific condition of having a ready recipient. The hadith underscores the practical responsibility of the payer to ensure the alms are not commingled with personal assets while awaiting distribution.
